title: Introduce gpu-nodepool-operator Terraform module to unify Karpenter + ASG failover in Private VPC
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Background: Private (VPC) customers require predictable GPU capacity with best-effort cost optimization. Today we have multiple ad-hoc Terraform modules for GPU ASGs and separate Karpenter bootstrap bits. That fragments lifecycle, complicates upgrades (NVIDIA driver changes, AMI rotation), and makes health checks inconsistent across node types. Goal: create a single reusable Terraform module 'gpu-nodepool-operator' that declares GPU node pools in Private, supports Karpenter provisioning as the primary path with an ASG fallback policy, exposes granular control for driver install strategy, healthchecks, and upgrade orchestration. Scope: module will live in infra/terraform/modules/gpu-nodepool-operator (registry-style inputs), provide outputs for NodeGroup identifiers and autoscaler hooks, integrate with customer VPC subnet selection, IAM roles, and KMS for any secrets. Key design decisions and trade-offs: - Driver installation: support two modes via module flag 'driver_install_mode': 'ami-baked' (preferred for performance) and 'daemonset' (fallback for rapid upgrades / mixed customer constraints). We will not force a single strategy since customers are heterogeneous. - Autoscaling model: Karpenter as primary with dedicated provisioner config (taints, labels, GPU instance selectors). ASG fallback implemented as a separate Terraform-managed AutoScaling Group with Lifecycle Hooks that activate only when Karpenter capacity falls below a configured threshold. This avoids double-provisioning while providing guaranteed capacity for SLA customers. - AMI management: provide optional Packer integration via pipeline link; module will accept AMI id input and validate via data source. We will not bake AMIs inside the module to keep CI separation. - Healthchecks: node-level healthchecks combine Kubernetes NodeReadiness, NVidia GPU driver metrics from node-exporter/gpu_exporter, and cloud-level instance status checks. Healthchecks will emit Prometheus metrics and CloudWatch custom metrics for alerting. - Upgrades: provide a documented rolling upgrade plan that uses node pool semantics: cordon->drain->terminate/remove from ASG or allow Karpenter to replace. Support preflight checks and dry-run mode. - Security: IAM roles, OIDC trust setup, and KMS usage documented. Because private deployments may be air-gapped, the module includes flags to disable public endpoints and use private SSM endpoints. Implementation notes: - Terraform inputs include: name, vpc_id, subnet_ids, gpu_instance_types (list), min/max/desired, driver_install_mode, karpenter_provisioner_config (map as JSON string), asg_fallback_enabled, asg_threshold_percent, ami_id, kubelet_extra_args, tags, kms_key_arn. - Outputs include: nodepool_id, asg_name, karpenter_provisioner_name, instance_profile_arn. - We will provide example root module for a full Private stack (examples/private-gpu-nodepool.tf). - Tests: unit testing via Terratest + integration using a small dev VPC and spot instance types in non-prod. Also automated plan checks in CI to prevent destructive changes to existing ASGs unless explicitly approved. - Observability: hook into existing Redwood Console metrics via telemetry schema: nodepool:<name>:gpu_utilization, nodepool:<name>:driver_ready_ratio, nodepool:<name>:unhealthy_nodes_count. Acceptance criteria are below.

2025-02-17 - Diego Morales: Proto design reviewed. Decided to support both amiga-baked and daemonset driver strategies. Raised concern about AMI rotation automation; recommended leaving that to Packer pipeline.

2025-02-20 - Arjun Patel (SRE): SRE requested explicit lifecycle hooks for ASG termination to run pre-terminate cleanup and to publish node termination events to internal SNS topic. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-02-25 - PM review (Lena Zhou): Confirmed customer impact and asked for a migration path doc for existing customers using old gpu-nodegroup modules.
2025-02-28 - Diego Morales: WIP PR opened with initial module scaffolding and examples. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1348 (do not merge).
2025-03-03 - Security (Maya R.): Preliminary security review requested; flagged KMS and IAM role scoping to be tightened. Security review scheduled for 2025-03-06.

steps: 1) Merge prototype module into infra/modules/gpu-nodepool-operator with basic inputs and outputs
2) Add example root module and Terratest integration in infra/tests/gpu-nodepool
3) Run security review and tighten IAM/KMS policies per feedback
4) Iterate on driver_install_mode support and validate both AMI-baked and DaemonSet workflows
5) Implement ASG fallback lifecycle hooks and test failover scenarios in dev account
6) Create migration guide and run one canary migration for existing private customers
7) Add monitoring metrics and Console integration, then ship to private-runtime-2025.03
acceptance_criteria: Module published in infra repo and referenced by example private stack
Karpenter provisioning works end-to-end for at least two GPU instance types with expected taints and labels
ASG fallback activates when Karpenter cannot provision and respects asg_threshold_percent setting
Driver install mode validated for both 'ami-baked' and 'daemonset' in integration tests
Automated CI plan check prevents accidental AMI changes without explicit approval
Healthchecks emit metrics to Prometheus and CloudWatch and trigger alerts when driver_ready_ratio < 90%
Security review completed and IAM/KMS concerns addressed
